params.body:
Replaces #807, which CI refused for two reasons that had nothing to do with the screen and everything to do with the migration. Both came from copying the Werking migration of a week earlier without reading what had changed since.

- It fell back to `parent_id = 0` when it could not find a parent, which puts an administrator page in the top bar. R P2-12.3 exists because that bar stops fitting on 1440 px.
- It wrote the menu name into `language_lines`. Menu names moved to `resources/lang/<taal>/menu.php` on 19 September, and `MenuNamesTest` was written that day precisely because Werking stood in the bar as "Menu.operations". I reproduced the bug the test was written to prevent.

Now: no parent means no item, never a top-level one, and the name lives in the four language files. A screen missing from the menu is a smaller problem than a screen that breaks the menu for everyone. `AnAdminScreenNeverLandsInTheTopBarTest` pins all three, so the next copy of this migration fails locally instead of in CI.

The rest is unchanged from #807 and repeated here.

## A third screen

Three screens are about the platform itself and about nobody's cars, and until now there were two. Inzichten says how the platform does as a business, over months and years. Werking says whether the machine moves right now. What was missing is the traffic in between: how much work actually goes through the platform, and when.

The gap was already named. The Werking blade says, in so many words, that "who is inside and who calls the API" does not belong there, that it is drukte and not werking, and that it stays as one line without a table until this screen exists.

## It measures nothing

No new column, no new logging, no write on any request. Every number comes from a trace the work itself left behind: a vehicle entered, an offer, an order form, a lead, a bid, a Car-Pass, VIN or AutoConnect lookup. That is why the screen reaches back over the whole history on the day it opens instead of starting empty and being useful in a month.

On production the whole thing answers in about 150 ms, so the five-minute cache is mostly politeness.

## What it shows

- **The week, with last week beside it.** 595 handlings by 62 garages means nothing until you see the 392 by 51 that came before.
- **Per day over 30 days**, with every day present. A day on which nothing happened is a zero and not a gap: a series that skips quiet days draws a quiet Sunday as if it never existed.
- **What it consists of**, each kind against the same length of time before it.
- **When the work happens**, per weekday and per hour over 90 days. One month cannot tell you anything about a Tuesday. (Thursday is the busiest day; the peak is at 16h.)
- **Which garages carry it**, and **which have gone quiet** this month.

## Two things it refuses to show, and says so on the screen

- **Vehicles that were edited.** `vehicles.updated_at` is overwritten, so a car edited five times keeps only the last one. A daily series of that would be roughly right for this week and badly wrong for last month — the kind of number that looks fine and lies.
- **Sign-ins per day.** Only the last sign-in per user is kept (`users.last_login_at`, since 19 September 2026). That answers "who has not been back" and never "how many people signed in on Tuesday", and a user without one has not been seen since we started looking rather than never been here.

Photos are on the screen but not counted as handlings: one saved car produces twenty rows, so adding them in turns the total into a photo counter with some work mixed in.

## Deliberately not in here

Werking still carries its "who is inside" and partner-API lines. Moving them over is the natural next step and touches that screen's tests, so it is its own change.

## Verified

New chapter R P3-16 with six rules. Full suite: 2,164 tests, with only the two known `ListPageHeadersTest` cases failing, which fail the same way without this change because those tables are empty in my local database. `phpstan` green over the project, `pint` green.
params.title: Activity: how much work goes through the platform
